issues.detail: Lacks comprehensive coverage of error scenarios (failed inserts, connection failures, concurrent write conflicts) and edge cases (clock skew, very stale clients) beyond basic reconnection sync.

PostgreSQL-specific syntax and patterns (BIGSERIAL, gen_random_uuid, TIMESTAMPTZ, uuidv7, EXPLAIN) require significant adaptation for MySQL, MongoDB, and other databases despite acknowledging their existence.
Example section provides prompts and descriptions rather than concrete demonstrations with sample input data and realistic query output.

scenarios.name: message-history-cursor-pagination
scenarios.rationale: Response A meets all four rubric requirements exactly: BIGSERIAL primary key, (channel_id, id DESC) index, keyset filtering with id < cursor and id > cursor, and cursor metadata format. Response B provides a valid cursor-pagination design but uses MongoDB ObjectId instead of BIGSERIAL, indexes (conversationId, createdAt) instead of the required pattern, and uses MongoDB query syntax ($lt) rather than the specified SQL keyset approach.

scenarios.name: unread-count-badge
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly matches the rubric's SQL requirements (last_read_message_id tracking, GROUP BY channel_id, id > filter pattern, 99+ optimization), while Response A uses MongoDB/NoSQL entirely and omits all SQL-specific patterns. Response B's only gap is not explicitly explaining why per-message read status is inefficient; Response A misses the entire technical direction.

scenarios.name: reconnection-sync-protocol
scenarios.rationale: Response A directly implements all rubric requirements: client sends per-channel lastMessageIds, server queries id > lastMessageId per channel, includes gap detection with 200-message threshold, and returns per-channel data with hasMore. Response B discusses 5 general sync patterns but implements single-cursor (not per-channel) sync, lacks gap detection logic, and doesn't match the specified return structure—it goes in a different architectural direction than the rubric requires.
